message:
Capture has choice while power and sensing have only one working means each, so the plan is not yet selectable. Plain words first for Aero-Rotor Lead, Structures-Survival Engineer, Power-Systems Engineer and Safety-Control Integrator: hold and brake have at least two working means but generate, feed and sense do not. The hold thrust (E22) is 37.3 N and the tip speed (E13) is 3.15e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, with trip target 315 RPM, and the two weakest functions are feed and sense because regulation droop and sensor thresholds have no numbers. Aero-Rotor Lead and Structures-Survival Engineer still owe a second means or explicit no-field statement for generate, feed and sense, and Power-Systems Engineer and Safety-Control Integrator will each bring one distant analogy with written mapping in cycle 2 for feed and for sense.

Sizes, loads and energies check against everyday things and fit the box in diameter but not yet along the shaft. Plain words first: the spinning disc leaves a finger width per side, pushes like a heavy shopping bag, makes laptop-level power at safe touch volts and stops well inside the limit. The 40 cm rotor in the 45 cm cube (C9) leaves 2.50 cm per side against the post tip deflection (E26) of 0.516 mm, the survival thrust (E22) of 37.3 N is about 3.80 kg weight, the shaft power (E12) of 34.7 W versus net power (E38) of 26.0 W differ by diode and regulator loss, and the open-circuit volts (E36) of 14.3 V with dump heat (E39) of 51.1 W are household-bulb level for seconds. The critical quantity nobody computed is parked aerodynamic torque at 22 m/s with stalled blades plus axial stack length inside the cube and brake temperature rise, and the two torque values for one hold quantity disagree with the friction hold (C21) of 0.400 N·m below the wind torque in the runaway check (E48) of 0.480 N·m.

There are no open blocking objections on the board to resolve, and the brake conflict must be settled by Safety-Control Integrator with help from Aero-Rotor Lead. Plain words first: all four not-ready votes agree with the evidence because selection and restart proof are missing. The combined stop simulation (E47) crosses below 10 percent in 1.65 s against 10 s and sits at 0.00 RPM at 10 s while electrical-only (E48) fails at 9.12e+03 RPM, so I answer Aero-Rotor Lead, Structures-Survival Engineer, Power-Systems Engineer and Safety-Control Integrator that none is ready until the Manager selects, interfaces are shown in the side-view shutdown layout (E50), and bench tests for power curve and re-latch restart are named.

RECORD: Decided is 40 cm three-blade fixed-pitch rotor with soft stall, stiff post mount, direct-drive outrunner with bridge and dump resistor, and latched trip with spring disc plus dump; numbers standing are 3.27 W at 5 m/s (E11), 34.7 W shaft and 26.0 W net at 11 m/s (E12)(E38), 1.43e+03 to 3.15e+03 RPM (E14)(E13), 37.3 N thrust and 13.1 N·m moment (E22)(E23), 0.516 mm deflection and 16.6 MPa stress (E26)(E27), 14.3 V top and 6.50 V low (E36)(E37), and 1.65 s stop (E47); still open are second means for generate feed sense, parked-torque versus 0.400 N·m hold, axial length and temperature, selection and bench tests owed by named members in cycle 2.

Note on Aero-Rotor Lead: Strong power and speed sizing with sources, still owes explicit interface to brake hold and parked-torque help.
Note on Structures-Survival Engineer: Strong thrust deflection and clearance margins, still owes axial stack sum and brake-rail compatibility.
Note on Power-Systems Engineer: Strong voltage and dump sizing, still owes regulation numbers and second feed analogy.
Note on Safety-Control Integrator: Strong latched trip and timed stop proof, still owes parked-hold reconciliation and restart proof.

Not ready, because no function is selected and parked hold, axial fit and bench tests are unsettled.
